paragraphs: Friend, this chapter is about a family that runs out of everything. A famine sends Naomi's family to Moab, and then she loses her husband and both of her sons (Ruth 1:1-5). By the time she turns for home, she says, "I went away full, but the LORD has brought me back empty" (Ruth 1:21). I think this one hurts, and it's okay to say so.

But look at the road, because Naomi hears that the LORD has attended to His people by providing them with food, and that news is what gets her moving (Ruth 1:6). Then Ruth, a Moabite, refuses to leave her side: "your people will be my people, and your God will be my God" (Ruth 1:16). Orpah goes back and Ruth clings, and that's the whole turn of the chapter, one woman choosing to stay when everything says go. That's loyalty, baker, and I don't mean the kind you see in a group chat.

So here's the big idea: Naomi walks into Bethlehem feeling empty, and she says so out loud, but she doesn't walk in alone. Ruth is right beside her, and they arrive "at the beginning of the barley harvest" (Ruth 1:22). The bitterness is real, and so is the food coming in. Hang on to your apron, friend, because this story is NOT done.
